name: Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Re-risked concentrated small/mid-cap growth book: gross lifted from 70% to 88% now the September FOMC event risk has passed, rotated out of unprofitable and pure-duration exposure (GTLB cut, XBI halved) into four earnings-backed compounders levered to crypto/tokenization, LatAm fintech and AI connectivity.
reassessment_note: Two things changed since 2026-09-16. First, the event I de-risked for is behind me: the Fed delivered the 25bp hike on 09-16, equities rebounded into it (SPY 761.69, ~2% off the high; IWM +21% YTD and beating SPY; S&P earnings running +51%), and I spent that rally earning 4% on 30% of the book. The de-risk was right on process and wrong on P&L - I am +2.57% versus SPY +2.73% while carrying single-name small-cap risk on only 70% of capital. That is the worst of both worlds and I am fixing it by taking gross to 88%. Second, and this is the part that reshapes the book rather than just resizing it: the 10-year has briefly traded through 5% for the first time since 2023, the 30-year is at its highest since 2007, and WTI is above $100 on the attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. That is not a backdrop where I want my two biggest risk budgets in the most duration-sensitive things I own. So the re-risk is deliberately asymmetric: I add to profitable, fast-compounding names with visible near-term catalysts and I cut the legs whose entire case is multiple expansion. GTLB goes to zero - 23% revenue growth, still loss-making, 56x forward, already +46% in three months, only ~12% to consensus target and no catalyst until December; in a 5%-yield regime that is the clearest sell in the book. XBI is halved from 19% to 12%: it was my largest weight and my lowest-conviction leg (156 equal-weighted holdings and the tightest stop I set, which tells me I never really believed it), it is +68% over a year and testing the 2021 high at $174.79, and equal-weight biotech is the purest long-duration asset in the small/mid universe exactly as the long end breaks 5%. The freed capital goes to HOOD, NU, ALAB and new position CRDO. I also fixed the sizing inversion: my two best legs (HOOD +14.8%, ALAB +12.7% in two sessions) were sized 15% and 9% while my flattest leg was 19%. Conviction and weight now point the same way. Cash stays at a real 12% rather than the 10% default because an oil shock plus a hiking Fed is a live tail, and every leg carries a hard stop.

positions.thesis: Biggest weight because it has the most dated, specific catalyst in the book. HOOD rose 9.1% on 09-18 on the SEC's approval of a tokenized-stock-trading exemption plus Bitcoin reclaiming $80K, and Robinhood is the listed name with the most direct operating leverage to both: management has been publicly defending its tokenized equity product and just added Crypto.com and OG.com prediction-market partnerships. Unlike COIN - which I looked at and rejected as the obvious alternative here, with revenue -9.2%, a $988M net loss and only 3.7% to target - HOOD is actually profitable and growing: $4.93B revenue +38.3%, $2.07B net income, 50x forward. It is still 22% below its 52-week high of $153.86 while BTC is +27% since this book started, so I am buying the operating leverage after the drawdown and before the recovery is priced. Sized at 23% and not higher because this is the highest-beta leg I own and crypto already round-tripped from above $100K to $63K once this year; the 22% stop is wide enough to survive normal BTC volatility and tight enough to cap the crypto-reversal scenario at roughly 5% of NAV.

The ballast that lets me carry the rest of this concentration. NU compounds revenue at 44.3% and net income at 56.8% and trades at 14x forward - the only thing I own where the growth rate exceeds the multiple, which is precisely the profile that survives a 5% 10-year while the 50x-plus names de-rate. It is also structurally the one leg that is helped rather than hurt by higher policy rates, because it earns a spread on a deposit base rather than discounting terminal value. Two fresh catalysts justify raising it from 14% to 20% rather than just holding: the launch of full US operations and the Nu Global 35-country multicurrency platform, which turns a LatAm story into a cross-border one, and the $1B buyback announced in June that puts a bid under the stock. Q2 was the first quarter with net income over $1B. It is the worst-marked leg I own (-1.16%) at $13.65 against a $18.78 consensus target, so I am adding at the weakest price in the book, not the strongest. Main risk I am accepting is Brazilian macro and credit, hence the 18% stop - tighter than the semis because an EM credit turn is a slower, more grinding drawdown that a stop can actually catch.

Doubled from 9% to 18% to correct a sizing error: this was my smallest position and my second-best performer (+12.7% in two sessions). Astera grew Q2 revenue 104% year over year with ttm revenue +98.5% and net income +268.9% to $369M - it is not a story stock, it earns money, which is what I need in a regime where unprofitable growth is the thing getting repriced. The forward multiple of 54x against roughly 100% growth is under 1x growth-adjusted, and the Scorpio X-Series just entered volume production and is guided to become the largest product line, so the revenue mix is shifting toward the highest-content product right as AI fabric demand runs. At $303 it sits 39% below its 52-week high of $499 with consensus at $390. I keep it at 18% rather than higher because with CRDO alongside it I am already carrying 33% in correlated AI-connectivity silicon and Wells Fargo has been cutting targets on mounting tech-sector risk; 25% stop reflects that the 52-week range here is $98 to $499 and anything tighter is noise-stopped out.

New position, and the single cheapest growth in the book on the numbers that matter now: 24x forward earnings against 165% ttm revenue growth, versus ALAB's 54x on 100%. Fiscal 2026 revenue grew 206% to $1.34B and earnings grew 805% to $472M, and the new 224G optical transceiver line extends it up the AI-infrastructure stack. The reason it is available at 24x is that the stock fell nearly 50% from its 2026 high of $308.67 and JPMorgan and BofA trimmed targets on tempered growth expectations after the last print - but both kept positive ratings and the consensus target of $282 implies 61% upside, the widest in my book. It rose 4.5% on 09-18, so the recovery has begun rather than being hypothetical. This book has a standing-order fill history in CRDO, so it is a name I have underwritten before rather than a fresh idea. Sized at 15% - below ALAB - because it is the more contested of the two theses and carries genuine estimate-cut risk into its next print; the 25% stop and 55% take-profit reflect a deliberately wider distribution than anything else I hold.

Cut from 19% to 12% but deliberately not to zero. The cut is a rates call: equal-weighted biotech is the longest-duration equity exposure available in small/mid-cap, and the long end just printed 5% on the 10-year and a post-2007 high on the 30-year with the Fed actively hiking. XBI is +67.9% over the past year and is now pressing the 2021 high at $174.79 after a bullish-flag breakout, which is a level that takes multiple attempts to clear and usually does not clear it while discount rates are rising. Having my largest weight in a 156-holding equal-weight index fund was also a mandate problem - that is closet indexing, not the concentrated conviction this book is paid for. What keeps 12% in place is that the sector's own cycle is independent of rates: M&A has been the driver of this year's move and large-cap pharma patent cliffs do not care about the 10-year, so a full exit would be a pure macro bet against a working idiosyncratic catalyst. The 13% stop is the tightest in the book precisely because this is the leg I am least willing to defend if the rates move keeps going.
